title: LockFee: Refundable Transaction Admission via Time-Locked Collateral
venue: IEEE International Conference on Decentralized Applications and Infrastructures
summary: Studies transaction admission through temporarily locked, refundable collateral: users bear the opportunity cost of capital instead of an irreversible base-admission fee.
abstract: LockFee requires an admitted transaction to lock collateral for a fixed duration and later returns the nominal principal. Users bear opportunity cost and asset risk. In an equal-size-transaction model, the paper relates the capital needed to occupy all admission slots to throughput, collateral, and lock duration. A baseline combines this rule with inflation-funded validator rewards and analyzes participation and self-spam resistance. Removing the base-admission fee channel does not remove every source of value from transaction ordering.
